name: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
description: Shopska salad, Bulgaria's real national salad, depends on real grated (not crumbled) sirene cheese - real technique uses a box grater so the cheese falls in light, fluffy shreds that form an airy blanket over the vegetables, slowly soaking up the tomato juices and oil beneath, rather than scattered crumbles.
steps_detailed: Toss the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, and onion with the olive oil and vinegar.
Grate the feta on the large holes of a box grater directly over the top, so it falls in light, fluffy shreds forming a real blanket over the vegetables, rather than crumbling it by hand.

name: Bulgarian Banitsa
description: Banitsa, a coiled phyllo pastry filled with real yogurt and cheese, is a genuine symbol of Bulgarian culture, traditionally served at Christmas and New Year, sometimes with small charms called kusmeti tucked inside - real technique rolls the filled phyllo into a long log first, then coils it into a tight spiral before baking.
steps_detailed: Whisk the yogurt, egg, and crumbled feta together.
Brush each phyllo sheet with melted butter, spread a thin line of the filling along one edge, and roll into a long, thin log.
Coil each rolled log into a tight spiral, arranging the coils together in a round baking dish.
Brush the top with more melted butter and bake at 375F (190C) for 40-45 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Bulgarian Tarator
description: Tarator, a cold cucumber and yogurt soup, is a beloved Bulgarian summer staple, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water so the soup doesn't turn watery.
steps_detailed: Salt the grated cucumber and let sit 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Whisk the yogurt with the garlic and olive oil, then stir in the cucumber, walnuts, and dill.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving.

name: Bulgarian Kavarma
description: Kavarma, meat and vegetables slow-baked together in a clay pot, is a genuine Bulgarian comfort dish, real technique layering everything into the pot and baking low and slow rather than stirring on the stovetop.
steps_detailed: Layer the beef, bell pepper, onion, tomatoes, and oregano in a baking dish.
Cover tightly and bake at 350F (175C) for 1.5-2 hours, until the beef is completely tender.

name: Bulgarian Kyufte
description: Kyufte, grilled meat patties seasoned with real cumin and a genuine soda-water addition, is a beloved Bulgarian dish, real technique using sparkling water to keep the patties genuinely light and tender.
steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the onion, cumin, and garlic, and let rest 15 minutes.
Shape into flattened oval patties.
Grill or pan-sear, 4-5 minutes per side, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Bulgarian Lyutenitsa
description: Lyutenitsa, a real roasted red pepper and tomato relish, is one of Bulgaria's most essential condiments, real technique roasting the peppers until the skins char fully for genuine smoky depth.
steps_detailed: Roast the peppers at 450F (230C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the skins are fully charred and blistered.
Let cool slightly, then peel and blend with the tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until thickened.

description: Bob chorba, a hearty white bean soup, is a genuine Bulgarian staple, real technique building depth from a real sautéed onion, carrot, and paprika base.

name: Bulgarian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Bulgaria's Black Sea coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

description: A simple roasted walnut snack, common across Bulgaria.
steps_detailed: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

description: Bulgaria is genuinely the birthplace of the specific bacterial strain used to culture real Bulgarian yogurt, and eating it simply with honey is a beloved everyday breakfast.
